page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 virtual server provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system RAM. Designed with a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no onboard GPU accelerators and features no local ephemeral storage, requiring attached network persistent disks for operating system and data storage needs.

With its dedicated core model, the n4d-highcpu-8 provides consistent CPU execution resources without core throttling or shared-thread interference. Allocating 16.0 GB of RAM against 8 vCPUs offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require higher processing concurrency without paying for idle system memory. The primary tradeoff is the absence of high-speed local NVMe storage and large RAM allocations, which limits use cases requiring massive in-memory caching or intensive local scratch space.

This resource profile fits compute-centric workloads where task execution scales with vCPU thread count. Typical applications include continuous integration build runners, batch data transformations, video transcoding, distributed web serving layers, and compute-focused microservice backends.

The server is well suited for running continuous integration pipelines, software compilation, batch processing jobs, multi-threaded worker nodes, and scalable web application backends.
